question:
A hydrogen discharge tube emits the Balmer lines corresponding to the transitions $n=3\to 2$ and $n=4\to 2$.

This light is sent through a thin prism of apex angle $A=5^{\circ}$ placed at a distance $L=1.0\,\text{m}$ from the cathode of a photoelectric cell. The prism is oriented close to minimum deviation so that the thin-prism formula $\delta\approx (n-1)A$ (with $A$ in radians) may be used.

For the wavelengths corresponding to the two Balmer transitions, the refractive indices of the prism material are:
$$n_{(3\to 2)}=1.500,\qquad n_{(4\to 2)}=1.510.$$

After refraction, the two emergent beams fall on the cathode at two separated points. Using a movable slit, each beam is allowed to illuminate the cathode separately, and the corresponding stopping potentials $V_{s(3\to 2)}$ and $V_{s(4\to 2)}$ are measured.

The work function of the cathode metal is $\phi=1.60\,\text{eV}$. Ignore contact potential. Use Bohr energy levels $E_n=-\dfrac{13.6}{n^2}\,\text{eV}$ and the photoelectric relation $eV_s=h\nu-\phi$.

Find the correct pair $(\Delta x,\, V_{s(4\to 2)}-V_{s(3\to 2)})$, where $\Delta x$ is the linear separation of the two spots on the cathode (use small-angle approximation $\Delta x\approx L\,\Delta\delta$).
